  "summary": "S1 [fact] Extend the existing Node.js ticket service with bulk reassignment and escalation; the service checkout is the delivery target, and discovery must inspect the earlier assignment run and any recovery context. S2 [fact] POST /tickets/reassign accepts from and to, requires different agents, moves all matching open or in-progress tickets, and returns moved and their IDs in ID order; discovery resolves existing validation and contract conventions. S3 [fact] Each moved ticket triggers the existing single-assignment notification for its new agent. S4 [fact] An open, unassigned, urgent ticket older than ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES, default 60, triggers an escalation notification to ONCALL; unset ONCALL disables escalation; discovery resolves ticket representations, scheduling, and notification integration. S5 [fact] Each ticket may be escalated at most once across service restarts; discovery must establish durable state, concurrency, and notification failure behavior. S6 [fact] Preserve all existing service behavior, including assignment, and keep the existing tests passing. S7 [fact] Add node:test coverage for the new behavior. [Assumption] Consumers use the existing service entry points and identity, visibility, and shared-state rules; discovery must establish the actors, runtime identification, state ownership and lifetime, session and device sharing, hidden data, and available runtime facilities. [Assumption] Existing ticket state and any durable escalation marker follow the service's established lifecycle; discovery must establish what ends that state and what survives restart. [Boundary] Intake implements nothing and adds no product scope; no deployed target or release authority is named. [Visibility] In an isolated run, the source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; a deployed outcome is visible only after an authorized release. [Discovery leads, not verified facts] Inspect the private service repository, prior-run context, ticket and assignment routes, models, storage, notifications, configuration, tests, package scripts, and available project documentation or owners; no team, workspace, channel, internal site, or owner is identified in the request. Treat agent, urgent, open, in-progress, ticket age, and ID order as terms to resolve against evidence. Store any sensitive locator only in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/. [Risk] Duplicate escalation after restart or concurrent checks, missed notification on failure, and regression of assignment are principal concerns; discovery must examine them before implementation."
